title: Roast Pork Loin with Apples & Onions
subtitle: a brown sugar and dried-herb rubbed pork roast over sweet apples and onions, with a quick pan sauce
imageAlt: Sliced roast pork loin with soft apple and onion wedges and a little jug of pan sauce on a white platter
servingsNote: dinner for two, plus 4 portions for sandwiches and lunches

breakdown: Brown sugar, oil, dried herbs, spices, cornstarch

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen roast? Thaw it in the fridge, about 10 hours per kg.
Oven at 220°C (425°F) to brown, then 180°C (350°F) to finish.
Pull it at 71°C (160°F) on an instant-read thermometer. Pork loin is lean and dries out past that.

items.name: Gala apples
items.note: cored and cut in 8 wedges each

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Pat the roast dry with paper towel.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Mix the salt, pepper, dried thyme, dried sage, garlic powder and brown sugar. Rub the roast with the oil, then with the seasoning on all sides.

steps.title: Into the pan
steps.text: Toss the apple and onion wedges with the melted butter in a roasting pan or 9×13 dish. Push them to the sides and set the roast in the middle, fat side up.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Lower the oven to 180°C (350°F), pour the broth over the apples and roast 40–50 minutes, stirring the apples once, until a thermometer in the centre of the roast reads 71°C (160°F).

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Move the roast to a board, tent with foil and rest 10 minutes. Spoon the apples and onions into a serving dish and keep warm.

steps.title: Pan sauce
steps.text: Scrape the pan juices into a small saucepan with the broth and bring to a boil. Stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer 1 minute, until glossy. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: Slice the pork about 1 cm thick and serve with the apples, onions and sauce.

fixIt.fix: It went past 71°C. Slice thin and spoon the sauce over; pull it right at 71°C next time, as it climbs while resting.
Softer apples like McIntosh collapse. Gala, Honeycrisp or Ambrosia hold their shape.
Add a few spoonfuls of water or broth to the pan partway through.
Simmer 1–2 minutes more, or add another 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with cold water.

saleTip: Whole pork loins go on sale at No Frills around the holidays, often under $2.50/lb. Have the meat counter cut a 1.2 kg roast and chops from the rest, and freeze them.
swap: Bone-in pork loin roast (about 1.6 kg): same method, 55–70 minutes at 180°C (350°F) to 71°C (160°F), with the thermometer not touching the bone.
leftovers: Thin-sliced pork sandwiches with the apples, or chopped into fried rice.
doneness: 71°C (160°F) in the centre (Health Canada, pork). A little blush of pink at 71°C is safe. Reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested pork loin roast methods (Canadian Pork, Canadian Living): seared at high heat, finished at 180°C (350°F) to 71°C, with apples roasted alongside.
prepAhead: Rub the roast with the seasoning up to 1 day ahead and keep it uncovered in the fridge; it browns even better.
Cut the apples just before roasting so they don't brown.
reheat: Lay slices in a dish with a spoonful of sauce or broth, cover with foil and warm at 160°C (325°F) 15–20 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Salt, pepper and dried thyme on the pork, and the pan juices spooned over instead of a thickened sauce.

stepNotes.1: Basic: rub with oil, salt, pepper and dried thyme only.
stepNotes.6: Basic: skip the sauce; spoon the pan juices over the slices.

fancy.note: A maple glaze for the last 15 minutes and a splash of cream in the sauce.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: brush the maple syrup over the roast for the last 15 minutes.
stepNotes.6: Fancy: stir in the cream after the cornstarch and simmer 1 minute more.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Fan the slices over the apples and onions on a warm platter and pour the sauce into a jug.

plating: Slices fanned over the apples so the glaze shows.

why.0-0: A dry roast browns in the hot first 15 minutes; a wet one steams.
why.0-7: A spoon of brown sugar helps the crust brown and echoes the apples.
why.1-0: The apples cook in the pork juices and turn into a soft, sweet side dish.

funFact: Canada changed its pork advice from 77°C to 71°C because modern pork is much leaner and safer. That's why a slightly pink centre is fine now.

keeps.note: freeze slices with a little sauce so they stay moist

pairs: creamy mash for the pan sauce
drink: A Gewürztraminer or a light red, or hot apple cider.
